findings.passage: Election integrity should not be a partisan weapon. It should mean respecting legitimate election results, protecting every lawful vote and holding fraud accountable wherever it occurs — even when the person committing it is working for your own campaign.
findings.note: Letter to the editor signed by Mullock, answering his opponent's call for election integrity. He defines election integrity as respecting results, protecting lawful votes and punishing fraud. He names no ID or citizenship rule. The letter also covers a convicted operative who cast fraudulent mail-in ballots.

findings.passage: Callaway later pleaded guilty to procuring and casting fraudulent mail-in ballots in that election and was sentenced to two years in federal prison.
findings.note: In the same signed letter, Mullock describes a mail-ballot fraud conviction of an operative paid by his opponent. It is a statement about fraud, not about ID rules.
